advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/justify treating only 204 as success in delete_comment, and confirm read-after-delete lag cannot cause a false 'target remains' abort on an actually-successful delete.
evidence: cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:130-146 returns raw status; only 204 is treated as unambiguous success in run() (`if status != 204:` branch)
cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:444: `if record.get("status_code") == 204 and result is None:` — only 204 counts as a clean completed outcome
Jira Cloud DELETE comment documents 204, but intermediaries can normalize/alter the status
advisory.finding: JiraCloudTransport.delete_comment reads response.status but for non-204 success codes (e.g. a proxy returning 200/202) the run loop classifies the outcome as 'ambiguous' and only accepts it if the post-delete re-capture shows the target absent; a successful delete reported as 202 with a slightly stale read-after would be journaled as ambiguous and could halt the run.
scenarios: A gateway returns 200/202 on a successful DELETE
Read-after-delete lag makes the target still appear present, producing a 'target remains' abort on a delete that actually succeeded

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a multi-page inventory fixture that repaginates (adjusts startAt/total) after delete to cover the real multi-page re-capture path.
evidence: tests/integration/test_cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:43-44: sets `page["total"] = total` for every page but leaves `startAt` unchanged
comment_echo_reclaim_manifest.py:370: `or start != expected_start` — production validator requires contiguous startAt matching cumulative counts
advisory.finding: The FakeJira test double's delete_comment recomputes each page's `total` after a delete but never adjusts per-page `startAt`, so a multi-page issue whose earlier page loses a comment will present startAt/total values that the production inventory_by_key pagination validator would reject; the crash/resume and post-delete-delta tests therefore only exercise single-page inventories and may not cover the real multi-page re-capture path.
scenarios: A bound issue has more than one comment page and a mid-page comment is deleted
Post-delete _capture re-fetch would have to renumber pages; the fake does not model this

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting JiraCloudTransport.from_environment raises CleanupError('JIRA_URL must be an absolute https URL') for a non-https scheme (http://...) and for a scheme-less/empty-netloc value.
evidence: cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py from_environment: 'parsed = urllib.parse.urlsplit(jira_url); if parsed.scheme != "https" or not parsed.netloc: raise CleanupError("JIRA_URL must be an absolute https URL")'
search for 'JIRA_URL must be an absolute' in tests/integration returned (no matches)
search for 'from_environment' in tests/integration returned (no matches)
All test JIRA_URL values are 'https://jira.example.test' (test_cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:1011,1047,1075,1113,1161); the missing-credentials test (line 1092) only drops JIRA_API_TOKEN
advisory.finding: The newly added JIRA_URL scheme/netloc validation in JiraCloudTransport.from_environment ('JIRA_URL must be an absolute https URL', raised when scheme != 'https' or netloc is empty) has no test. Concrete violating inputs such as JIRA_URL='http://jira.example.test' (non-https scheme) or JIRA_URL='jira.example.test' (scheme-less / empty netloc) are never exercised; every test that reaches from_environment supplies a valid 'https://jira.example.test', and test_cli_refuses_missing_credentials only omits JIRA_API_TOKEN. A regression that dropped or weakened this URL check (e.g. accepting http:// and sending Basic-auth credentials over cleartext) would not be caught.
scenarios: An operator or misconfiguration supplies an http:// or scheme-less JIRA_URL, or the https guard is later removed in a refactor
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized test over ['http://jira.example.test', 'jira.example.test', 'ftp://jira'] asserting from_environment raises CleanupError matching 'absolute https URL' and that no urlopen call is made.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Catch ReclaimError (or both CleanupError and ReclaimError) in cleanup_comment_echo_jira.main() so live-inventory validation failures produce the 'cleanup refused' exit 2 path.
evidence: infra/scripts/cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:660: `    except CleanupError as exc:` — only CleanupError is handled
comment_echo_reclaim_manifest.py:341: `raise ReclaimError("Jira inventory has an unsupported schema or source")`
`class CleanupError(RuntimeError)` and `ReclaimError` (imported from reclaim_bridge_history) are unrelated classes, so ReclaimError is not caught
blocking.finding: manifest_tools.inventory_by_key raises ReclaimError (from reclaim_bridge_history), which is not a subclass of CleanupError; main() only catches CleanupError, so a malformed/incomplete live Jira inventory surfaced during _validate_observation, _target_present, or _validate_authorized_delta escapes as an uncaught traceback with exit code 1 instead of the intended 'cleanup refused' exit code 2.
scenarios: Live Jira returns an inventory that fails pagination/schema validation during --execute after some deletes have occurred
Operator sees a raw traceback + exit 1 instead of the structured 'cleanup refused' message
blocking.suggested_fix: In main(), broaden the except clause to `except (CleanupError, manifest_tools.ReclaimError) as exc:` (or wrap inventory_by_key calls to re-raise as CleanupError).
